hookLine: For decades the drinking water at Camp Lejeune carried industrial solvents, the base measured them, wrote them down, and the taps stayed open.

HOOK.secondary: A Marine Corps drill instructor buries his nine-year-old daughter. He hears nothing about the water until August 1997.

OP.label: De-duplicated administrative claims, United States' notice to the court

OP.secondary: One federal court. One deadline: 30 October 2026.

ACT_1.secondary: Marine Corps family housing. Jerry Ensminger and his wife lived there from 1973 to 1975; she spent her first trimester there.

ACT_1.label: Jerry Ensminger's service in the United States Marine Corps

A dry-cleaning solvent that leaked into the aquifer feeding the Tarawa Terrace wells from ABC One-Hour Cleaners, off base
An industrial degreaser in the Hadnot Point system, with benzene and the products TCE breaks down into

Janey Ensminger was born in 1976, after the family left. Diagnosed with acute lymphocytic leukemia at six. Ill for nearly two and a half years.

ACT_1.quote: Janey died at 3:35 p.m. on 24 September 1985. She was only 9 years old.
ACT_1.attribution: Jerry Ensminger, sworn testimony to Congress, 12 June 2007

She dies on 24 September, aged nine
Her father first hears that the base water was contaminated

ACT_2.secondary: The Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry had proposed a childhood leukemia and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma study
Children exposed in the womb while their parents lived at Camp Lejeune between 1968 and 1985
Letters to the base, to Headquarters Marine Corps, to the Navy - returned partial, returned late, returned with the useful part removed
A retired drill instructor at a kitchen table in North Carolina, teaching himself to read a laboratory form
Mothers who had miscarried at Tarawa Terrace. Men from the barracks at Hadnot Point with kidney cancer at fifty. Families scattered to Ohio, Texas and Florida.

ACT_2.primary: NO LEGAL TRAINING. NO SCIENTIFIC TRAINING.
ACT_2.secondary: What he had instead was twenty-four and a half years of learning how a military bureaucracy moves paper

ACT_2.quote: What they have filled me with is a terrible resolve to expose their misconduct, their arrogance, and their incompetence. And I want to expose the truth.
ACT_2.attribution: Jerry Ensminger, sworn testimony to Congress, 12 June 2007

ACT_2.quote: It is time for the United States Marine Corps to live up to our motto, which is Semper Fidelis, which is Latin for 'always faithful.'
ACT_2.attribution: Jerry Ensminger, sworn testimony to Congress, 12 June 2007

ACT_3.secondary: A United States Army Environmental Hygiene Agency team from Fort McPherson, Georgia begins routine trihalomethane tests on Camp Lejeune water systems. The contamination was too high for the test to be completed.

ACT_3.quote: Water is highly contaminated with low molecular weight halogenated hydrocarbons.
ACT_3.attribution: handwritten remark, Hadnot Point sample form, 30 October 1980 - document CLW 0436

ACT_3.quote: Heavy organic interference at CHCL2BR. You need to analyze for chlorinated organics by GC/MS
ACT_3.attribution: U.S. Army laboratory, 29 December 1980 - document CLW 0438

ACT_3.secondary: Samples of the same system, and the same instruction again: analyze for chlorinated organics by GC/MS

ACT_3.quote: Water highly contaminated with other chlorinated hydrocarbons (solvents)!
ACT_3.attribution: U.S. Army laboratory analytical result form, samples 9 March 1981, Hadnot Point - document CLW 0443

ACT_3.label: It sat in a government file until a retired drill instructor asked for it

ACT_3.secondary: Co-owner Mike Hargett telephones the base's own supervising chemist: high levels of volatile organic compounds in both the Hadnot Point and Tarawa Terrace systems

ACT_3.quote: These appeared to be at high levels and hence more important from a health standpoint than the total Trihalomethane content.
ACT_3.attribution: Bruce A. Babson, Grainger Laboratories, to the Commanding General, 10 August 1982

ACT_3.secondary: The contaminated wells at Hadnot Point come out of service. The most contaminated are shut down in February 1985.
The Tarawa Terrace treatment plant, the one that served the family housing, is closed
A federal criminal investigation looked for a conspiracy for eighteen months and found no violation of federal law. The Marine Corps' own review panel concluded the Corps had acted responsibly.

ACT_3.quote: one spokesperson for the hundreds of thousands of Marines, sailors, their families, and the loyal civilian employees who were unknowingly exposed
ACT_3.attribution: Jerry Ensminger, sworn testimony to Congress, 12 June 2007

ACT_3.secondary: No federal health agency has ever published one. The figure of around a million comes from a congressional hearing in 2010.

ACT_4.title: THE MAN BORN ON THE BASE

ACT_4.quote: 'You have male breast cancer' were the words which greeted me and my wife on our 18th wedding anniversary.
ACT_4.attribution: Mike Partain, sworn testimony to Congress, 16 September 2010

ACT_4.secondary: Son and grandson of Marine Corps officers. Conceived, carried and born at the base naval hospital in 1968, while his parents lived at Tarawa Terrace.
Negative for the hereditary breast cancer markers BRCA1 and BRCA2. He does not drink and does not smoke. Diagnosed in 2007, aged thirty-nine.

ACT_4.label: Men with male breast cancer and exposure to the Camp Lejeune water, as Partain told Congress
He located the first sixty-three himself, one at a time, by telephone and e-mail

ACT_4.secondary: One man's list, with no denominator and no control group. It was an alarm, and alarms are supposed to be crude.

items.label: Male breast cancer cases examined, published 2015

ACT_4.secondary: 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.97 for ever having been stationed at Camp Lejeune. On male breast cancer the results point both ways and nothing is established.

ACT_4.attribution: Mike Partain, sworn testimony to Congress, 16 September 2010, on the March 1981 remark

ACT_4.secondary: ATSDR withdraws its own 1997 public health assessment for Camp Lejeune. It had left benzene out.

items.label: Camp Lejeune Marines and sailors, 2014 mortality study

ACT_4.secondary: A cancer incidence study across the same two populations, following diagnoses from 1996 to 2017

ACT_4.quote: Increased risks of several cancers were observed among Marines/Navy personnel and civilian workers exposed to contaminated drinking water at Camp Lejeune compared with Camp Pendleton.
ACT_4.attribution: Bove et al., Environmental Health Perspectives, 24 October 2024

ACT_4.secondary: Sufficient evidence for causation: TCE and kidney cancer; TCE and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma; PCE and bladder cancer; benzene and the leukemias; vinyl chloride and liver cancer

ACT_5.secondary: A statute of repose runs from the defendant's last act and then expires, whether you know you were injured or not. The Supreme Court confirmed that federal environmental law does not override it.

ACT_5.label: Federal Tort Claims Act claims by Camp Lejeune families, with seventeen federal lawsuits

ACT_5.secondary: The Janey Ensminger Act: VA health care for fifteen specified conditions, for thirty days or more at Camp Lejeune between 1953 and 1987
The Camp Lejeune Justice Act, passed as section 804 of the PACT Act. File with the Navy, wait six months, then one district in eastern North Carolina.

ACT_5.quote: Any applicable statute of repose or statute of limitations... shall not apply to a claim under this section.

All four judges of the district sign a thirty-four-page order striking the jury demand. Every Camp Lejeune case will be tried by a judge.

A grid: $150,000 to $450,000 for the worst-exposed with the listed cancers, and another $100,000 if the claimant died

No court has ever ruled on whether the United States is liable. No individual has ever been publicly disciplined or prosecuted over the contamination.

ENDING.quote: Delay, deny, and wait 'til they die.
